Time: 2 min. Teaching intent: Open the hour and connect it to the week's decision.
Talk track: Identify die, interconnect, substrate, and thermal path on a package cross-section.
Expected answer / misconception: Students can name the outcome.
Visual: The visual previews the physical design or evidence chain.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Set the evidence contract.
Talk track: An annotated package cross-section and a list of unknowns.
Expected answer / misconception: A named artifact with source and a check, not an unsupported opinion.
Visual: Input, reasoning, and evidence are separate.
[Sources]
R1: TSMC Advanced Packaging Services | https://www.tsmc.com/english/dedicatedFoundry/services/advanced-packaging

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Can transistor design alone specify a package?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Interfaces, materials, assembly, and thermal boundaries remain.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R1: TSMC Advanced Packaging Services | https://www.tsmc.com/english/dedicatedFoundry/services/advanced-packaging
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: The die computes; the package connects, supports, protects, and removes heat. Trace the visual in order: die; interconnect; environment. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Trace a signal and a heat path from a compute die to the board and ambient.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R1: TSMC Advanced Packaging Services | https://www.tsmc.com/english/dedicatedFoundry/services/advanced-packaging
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Trace a signal and a heat path from a compute die to the board and ambient. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

R1: TSMC Advanced Packaging Services | https://www.tsmc.com/english/dedicatedFoundry/services/advanced-packaging
